title: Platform systems & services: runbooks, dashboards, how-tos, roadmap, and team wiki
author: Morgan Lee
body:
Summary

This page consolidates core platform engineering artifacts: systems & services inventory, standard runbooks, dashboards & alerting guidelines, common how-tos, recent retrospectives, and a near-term roadmap. It is intended to be the single reference for oncall, incident leads, and new platform engineers. Links to detailed runbooks and the team wiki are provided in Related pages.

1) Systems & services inventory

- Platform control plane (service name: platform-api) — REST/GRPC control API for job submission, queueing, and configuration.
  - SLO: availability 99.9% monthly; p95 request latency < 120ms for control plane API endpoints.
  - Owners: platform-api team (oncall @platform-api).
- Scheduler (service name: platform-scheduler) — handles job placement, GPU capacity accounting, and autoscaling signals.
  - SLO: 99.5% success for scheduling decisions under normal load.
  - Owners: infra-scheduler.
- Metric collector (platform-metrics) — aggregates Prometheus metrics and ships to long-term storage.
  - Retention: 90 days standard, 365 days for compliance metrics (paid addon).
- Auth & RBAC (platform-auth) — issues tokens, integrates with KMS, supports role-mapping for Dedicated/Private customers.
- CLI & SDK (redwoodctl and SDK libs) — developer-facing tools; release cadence: biweekly for SDKs.

For full inventory and service dependencies, see the team wiki and service graph dashboard (Grafana: Platform -> Service Dependency Graph).

2) Dashboards & alerts

Purpose: detect service degradation early, provide actionable signals that map to runbooks, and reduce noisy alerts.

Key dashboards (Grafana namespace: Platform):
- Platform Overview (dash id: platform_overview) — aggregated health, request rates, errors, cluster capacity, and deployment status.
- Control Plane Latency (platform_latency) — p50/p95/p99 latency by endpoint and route.
- Scheduler Health (platform_scheduler) — queue depth, scheduling latency, pending GPU memory, and backpressure metrics.
- Cost & Utilization (platform_cost) — GPU utilization by pool, GPU-hours consumed, and cost trend.
- Long-term Trend (platform_trends) — weekly summaries and anomaly detection.

Prometheus alerting guidelines (examples):
- platform_api_errors_high
  - Expr: sum(rate(platform_api_request_errors_total[5m])) by (job) > 5
  - Threshold: more than 5 errors/min sustained for 5 minutes for critical endpoints.
  - Severity: P1 (pager).
- platform_api_latency_p95
  - Expr: histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(platform_api_request_duration_seconds_bucket[5m])) by (le, endpoint)) > 0.12
  - Threshold: p95 > 120ms for control endpoints for 10m.
  - Severity: P2 (pager for repeated or correlated alerts).
- scheduler_queue_depth_high
  - Expr: sum(platform_scheduler_queue_depth) > 100
  - Severity: P1 when >100 sustained for 2 mins; P2 if 50-100 for 15 mins.

Alert lifecycle and ownership:
- Alerts must include a runbook link and suggested immediate remediation (see Runbooks section).
- Alert severities map to PagerDuty policies: P1 -> platform-core escalation, P2 -> service owner followup.
- Reduce noise by preferring rate-based alerts and grouping by cluster/region.

3) Runbooks (standardized template)

Every runbook must follow this template (title, impact, detection, owner, priority, immediate steps, diagnostic commands, remediation steps, rollback, postmortem link):

Example: platform-api partial outage (P1)
- Impact: control-plane requests return 5xx or time out; customer API calls failing to create jobs.
- Detection: platform_api_errors_high alert triggers; p95 latency > 120ms.
- Owner: platform-api oncall.
- Immediate steps (0-15m):
  1. Acknowledge alert in PagerDuty, create incident in Incident Manager.
  2. Check Platform Overview dashboard for correlated failures (downstream services, DB, auth).
  3. Run quick health checks: curl -sS https://platform-api.internal/health | jq .status
  4. If errors are DB-related, check DB failover or connection pool exhaustion.
- Diagnostic commands:
  - kubectl get pods -n platform -l app=platform-api -o wide
  - kubectl logs -n platform deploy/platform-api -c api --since=10m | tail -n 200
  - promql: sum(rate(platform_api_request_errors_total[5m])) by (endpoint)
- Remediation (15-60m):
  1. Scale up platform-api replicas or increase CPU requests if CPU throttling is observed.
  2. If a recent deploy is suspect, rollback to previous release: `kubectl rollout undo deployment/platform-api -n platform`.
  3. Apply emergency config: rotate connection pools or increase DB max connections as short-term mitigation.
- Post-incident: link to postmortem template and required fields (impact, timeline, root cause, action items).

Runbook ownership and review cadence:
- Owners must review runbooks quarterly or after any oncall incident.
- Changes must be recorded in the runbook changelog with author and date.

4) How-tos (common procedures)

- Adding a dashboard: Steps to create Grafana folder (Platform -> New Dashboard -> Add panels -> assign permission group platform-view). Include tags: `platform`, `service-name`, `region`.
- Defining an alert: Use Prometheus recording rules where possible, avoid firing directly on raw metrics. Provide alert annotation `runbook_url`.
- Deploying a safe rollback: Canary -> Monitor -> Rollout. Use the `redwoodctl rollout` command to perform canary and automatic rollback on error rate spike >2x baseline.
- Creating a new service: follow the Platform Service Onboarding checklist (register service in service-registry, add SLO, create default dashboards, create PagerDuty service). Checklist link in Related pages.

5) Retrospectives & continuous improvement

- Quarterly retrospective summary (last 3 incidents):
  - Q4 2025: Scheduler race condition causing delayed job assignment (action: add stronger leader election + integration tests).
  - Q1 2026: Metric collector partial outage due to storage throttling (action: increase buffer sizing and introduce backpressure handling).
  - Q1 2026: Several noisy alerts (action: reduce alert cardinality and introduce synthetic canaries).

Action items tracking:
- All action items must be entered into the platform backlog with owner and target date. Review at weekly platform cadence meeting.

6) Roadmap (next 6 months)

- Q2 2026 (current):
  - Migrate platform metrics to new long-term store with compression; target 10% cost reduction.
  - Implement rate-based autoscaling for scheduler to reduce P95 job latency by 20%.
  - Roll out standardized onboarding playbook and templates for new services.
- Q3 2026:
  - Introduce automated runbook drills (game days) and integrate outputs into runbooks.
  - Launch service-level cost dashboards per customer and per-pool.
- Q4 2026+:
  - Expand retained observability windows for enterprise customers and add audit trails for all runbook executions.

Roadmap notes:
- Prioritization is based on reducing operational toil (alerts, manual escalations) and improving cost efficiency.
- Feature owners are assigned in the roadmap board in Jira (board: PLAT-ROADMAP).

7) Team wiki & onboarding

- The team wiki contains: oncall rotation schedules, SLAs, service ownership list, runbook index, deployment checklists, incident playbooks, and links to further reading.
- New hire checklist (platform engineer):
  1. Access: get SSO + dev VPN + PagerDuty.
  2. Read the Platform Overview and top 5 runbooks.
  3. Complete a shadow oncall shift in the first 4 weeks.
  4. Deliver a short README update for a service in the service registry.

8) Ownership & contacts

- Platform Slack: #platform-ops (primary alert routing: @platform-oncall).
- Escalation: PagerDuty policy `Platform-Core-Escalation` (primary -> secondary -> eng-leads).
- Oncall rotation: 2-week rotations; handover template required for shift changes.

9) Appendix: useful queries and commands

- Prometheus: p95 latency
  `histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(platform_api_request_duration_seconds_bucket[5m])) by (le, endpoint))`
- Scheduler queue depth
  `sum(platform_scheduler_queue_depth)`
- Quick pod health
  `kubectl get pods -n platform -l app=platform-api -o wide`

Related pages:
- platform-operations-playbook-2026 (detailed operational playbook)
- platform-team-wiki-and-runbooks-2026 (service index and onboarding)
- platform-runbook-roadmap-2026 (detailed roadmap and owners)

If you are oncall and unsure, escalate to the platform-core pager and open an incident; do not manually restart stateful services without approval from the service owner.
